minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, February 19, 2020 in Community Room A located on the
first floor of City Hall. Commissioner Metcalf called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

  Present
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District 2
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Commissioner Vicki Banks, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
  Absent
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Ehrlich-Bell asked that the minutes reflect the correct spelling of her last name. Helen Lessick
corrected the spelling of Eilen Mena’s name under the Public Comments section.

  Commissioner Battle made a motion to approve the minutes from November 20, 2019. Commissioner
Metcalf seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Ehrlich-Bell, and Battle
  Nays: None

Special Presentation

  Peace, Love & Serve Inc., Yvette Baily’s presentation to be rescheduled for a later time.

  Eilen Mena from Zeal Press, a creative agency that represents Black Artists located at 6755 West Boulevard
spoke about their Artist Residency Program. She also asked for feedback or any grant suggestions that the
Commission may share with her. Sabrina Barnes informed Ms. Mena of the Percent for the Art Fund that
commission’s contracts for services and will be sure to keep her in the loop with future opportunities. Commissioner
Ehrlich-Bell asked if there are currently any showings. Ms. Mena stated her work is currently there and is planning for
an Open Studio event soon. She can be reached via email at: eilenitzelmena@gmail.com. Helen Lessick encouraged
the Commissioners to visit their website at ZealPress.com.

  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

Staff Report

  Helen Lessick presented a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend he Mayor and
Council Members award a contract to ShowPro.com in the amount of $25,000 to provide final design and, on
approval, install lighting for Skedans, the monumental public artwork at the La Brea Avenue entrance of City Hall.
Commissioner Battle asked if the funds will be coming out of the Public Art funds. Ms. Lessick stated yes.
Commissioner Banks asked if there were any other estimates. Ms. Lessick stated the city did receive another
estimate from an Inglewood firm but the panel did not recommend it. Sabrina Barnes shared that the panel reviewed
the bids and ShowPro was the winner based on the body and quality of work they proposed. Additionally, they have
lit other works in the city’s collection. Commissioner Banks asked if the lights will be on all night long. Ms. Lessick
stated they will be on a timer and are adjustable. Sabrina Barnes mentioned staff did consult with the artist before he
passed and the lighting will be complimentary and highlight the artwork, no colorful lighting. Commissioner Ehrlich-
Bell asked if the lighting will be solar powered. Ms. Lessick stated no and explained why is cannot be solar powered.

  Commissioner Banks made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Battle seconded and the staff
report was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Ehrlich-Bell, and Battle
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports Regarding the following Public Art Related Projects

  •  IGAP 2020: MLK Day public art by Michele Asselin and youth exhibited their Life’s Blueprint project on a vinyl
  banner which included a picture of their mentor and a written conversation with them. Banners were
  displayed along Market Street during the City’s annual MLK Celebration on January 18, 2020. The work is
  also displayed on the city’s public art website.
  •  IGAP 2019: Music composition and Performance – project has been cancelled due to the artist’s refusal to
  sign the city’s contract. Funds ($12,000) will go back to the Art Fund. Commissioner Banks asked why the
  artist wouldn’t sign the contract. Ms. Lessick stated she was essentially concerned with the amount of
  insurance the city required.
  •  Billboard Public Art discussion: Sabrina Barnes introduced the three-sided billboard that sits on top of the
  District 2 Community Center (on La Cienega and La Tijera Boulevards). Helen Lessick led a discussion
  regarding what the city may potentially commission to be displayed on two of the sides of the billboard, one
  being a digital design to be installed by Clear Channel at no cost. Information will be listed on the city’s art
  website when available. Ms. Barnes is working with Administration now to have something installed in the
  meantime so that it is not bare. IGAP may be able to commission a project that may possibly be funded by
  general funds. Commissioner Battle asked why Art Funds can’t be used. Ms. Barnes explained because it is
  private property. Commissioner Ehrlich-Bell asked if it can be something that refers people to the city’s art
  website and how long the art will be displayed. She also asked what the time frame will be and will the artist
  be compensated. Ms. Lessick stated yes to compensation and typically the time frame will be about 18
  months which includes Clear Channels final approval. We hope the art can be displayed for at least 4 to 6
  month, no longer than a year.

  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

  •  NEA 2021 Challenge discussion – National Endowment of the Arts has a $10,000 grant funding matching
  program. The city is proposing Inglewood Cultural Tourism which will promote the city’s website and our
  cultural partners including design studios, visual artists and music partners which is timely as Inglewood will
  begin preparing for the opening and closing ceremonies for the upcoming 2028 Summer Olympics. We will
  apply in March and receive notification in October to begin in January 2021. Project period is one year.

Public Comments

  Daniel Onsy from Wanda Wallace and Associates located in Inglewood will be selling their collection and
was interested to see what their institution can offer as a non-profit.

Commissioners’ Comments/Initiatives/Art Calendar

  Helen Lessick stated the LA Phil has free events available, see their website for more details.

  Commissioner Metcalf shared her recent experience when she attended a storyteller event and is going to
share it with the Senior Center. Commissioner Banks stated Inglewood resident, Michael McCarty is a great
storyteller.

  Commissioner Ehrlich-Bell asked if someone has an idea for a public art project that is community based,
would he just show up here. Ms. Barnes stated yes. However, it is preferred that they submit a written proposal to
the Department.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:50 p.m.
